line: Crowley’s Four of Swords: Truce, Chesed in the realm of the Intellect, Jupiter ruling Libra.

sections.title: What Crowley names
sections.line: The chapter name for the card. The second quotation gives the element of its suit.

quotes.quote: The Four of Swords is called Truce.
“Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air;

sections.title: Its place on the Tree and in the zodiac
sections.line: The Fours are attributed to Chesed. This card refers to Jupiter, who rules Libra in this decanate.

quotes.quote: These cards are attributed to Chesed.
Chesed refers to Jupiter who rules in Libra in this decanate.

sections.title: What it figures
sections.line: Crowley reads the card as authority in the intellectual world, a refuge from mental chaos.

quotes.quote: the card proclaims the idea of authority in the intellectual world
It represents a refuge from mental chaos, chosen in an arbitrary manner.
